items.stem: Who should enforce that an MCP client may only call the tools it is permitted to use?

options.text: The MCP server, on every tool call
options.rationale: Correct: authorization must be enforced server-side on each call, not assumed from the model.

options.text: The language model, by choosing not to call forbidden tools
options.rationale: Models can be manipulated; authorization cannot depend on model behaviour.

options.text: The end user, by reading the docs
options.rationale: Documentation is not an enforcement mechanism.

options.text: Nobody; MCP tools are safe by default
options.rationale: Exposed tools are not safe by default and must be authorized.

items.explanation: Correct: authorization must be enforced server-side on each call, not assumed from the model.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce the blast radius of an MCP tool? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Validate and constrain every tool argument before acting on it
options.rationale: Correct: validated, constrained inputs stop malformed or malicious arguments.

options.text: Grant each tool only the least privilege it needs
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege limits what damage a misused tool can do.

options.text: Give every tool full administrative access for convenience
options.rationale: Broad access maximises, not minimises, blast radius.
Dropping logs removes the audit trail needed to detect misuse.

items.explanation: Correct: validated, constrained inputs stop malformed or malicious arguments.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: What belongs in an MCP server's audit log?

options.text: Every tool call, including denied and failed ones, with who called it and the outcome
options.rationale: Correct: a complete audit trail records successes, denials and failures with attribution.
Omitting denials and failures hides exactly the events security review needs.
No audit trail means no way to detect or investigate misuse.
A banner is not an audit record of tool activity.

items.explanation: Correct: a complete audit trail records successes, denials and failures with attribution.
